Avogadro API All examplesServer molecule packs

Commands and imports

Reload molecule packs, inspect settings, export media, and import CAS substances. Server commands require permission level 2; export and CAS commands run locally on your client. The standalone console supports CAS commands only.

Server commands

Manage the server's molecules
Command Result
/avogadro reload Load current definitions and settings, then synchronize players. A failed reload keeps the previous snapshot.
/avogadro check Validate the combined collection and report counts and synchronization sizes without installing or sending it.
/avogadro explain <molecule-id> Show an installed molecule's effective settings and their sources; unreloaded edits are not included.

See server molecule packs for directories, precedence, and size limits.

Export commands

Save media from loaded molecules and items
Command Result
/avogadro export <molecule-id> [options] Export a rotating molecule as GIF or MP4.
/avogadro export all [options] Export one animated gallery; use --columns to set its layout.
/avogadro export item [held|namespace:item] [options] Export an item card. Held items retain metadata and custom names; registry IDs accept --meta.
/avogadro export 3d <molecule-id> --atom <number> [options] Export an atom; numbering starts at 1. Use --details true|false for its information panel.

Common options: --format gif|mp4, --width, --height, --fps, --speed (seconds per turn), --output, and --background "#RRGGBB"|none. Flags override saved preferences. MP4 requires FFmpeg and a solid background; existing files are never overwritten.

Use /avogadro export help for every option and limit, or /avogadro export status / /avogadro export cancel for the current job. See media exports for preferences and API examples.

Set up CAS lookup

In Minecraft, run /avogadro cas configure to enter your key in a masked prompt, then run /avogadro cas help.

For the standalone console, download the source distribution and launch avogadro-cas.cmd on Windows or sh avogadro-cas on Linux/macOS. Type help after it opens. The launcher prepares the Java authoring classpath using Gradle and Java 25 on first use. Internet access is required for that setup. It does not start Minecraft or include Minecraft binaries.

Run the launcher from the game directory to use that installation's configuration and cache. Use --directory to choose another definition output folder; it does not move the key or cache.

Set your API key

configure asks for your key without displaying it. Alternatively, set CAS_API_KEY before starting the game or tool, or put only the key in config/avogadro/cas-api-key. The environment variable takes precedence. Never paste a key into chat or a command argument. Tokens are personal; renew yours through CAS when it expires.

Commands execute locally. Your key is sent to CAS for API requests, never to a Minecraft server. Local imports do not override a remote server's synchronized definitions.

In-game commands

/avogadro cas help
/avogadro cas configure
/avogadro cas search <query> [--page <number>]
/avogadro cas names <CAS RN>
/avogadro cas preview <CAS RN>
/avogadro cas import <CAS RN> [options]
/avogadro cas import-list <file | JSON array> [options]
/avogadro cas status
/avogadro cas cancel
/avogadro cas cache open
/avogadro cas cache clear --yes

Console commands

Type these commands inside the interactive console. The cas prefix is optional for each command. Use exit to close the console. 

help
configure
search <query> [--page <number>]
names <CAS RN>
preview <CAS RN>
import <CAS RN> [options]
import-list <file | JSON array> [options]
status
cancel
cache open
cache clear --yes
exit

preview prints the validated molecule definition in the console. In Minecraft, it opens the molecule viewer.

Import options

Choose the output and name for an import
Option Effect
--directory <path> Choose the definition output folder.
--name <display name> Supply a custom display name.
--synonym <index> Select a numbered name from names.
--filename <filename> Choose the output filename.
--namespace <namespace> Choose the molecule namespace.
--id <resource identifier> Set the full identifier, such as mypack:aspirin.
--offline <saved CAS JSON> Read a saved detail response without a network request.
--dry-run Validate without saving a definition. Downloaded responses may still be cached.
--overwrite Allow replacing an existing definition file.

Existing files are preserved unless you supply --overwrite. --name, --synonym, --filename, --id and --offline apply to single imports. Batch imports use each substance's primary name.

Choose a name

names prints numbered choices. --synonym 0 selects the primary name; --synonym 1 selects the next listed name. Use the exact printed index, or supply your own name with --name. 

names 50-78-2
import 50-78-2 --name Aspirin --dry-run
import 50-78-2 --name Aspirin

Imports use Avogadro's Java molecule builder and validation. A CAS record must contain a structure that Avogadro supports before it can be saved as a molecule definition.

Import a list

import-list accepts a text file, a JSON array file, or an array typed directly into the command. Batches support up to 1,000 entries. Duplicates are removed while preserving order, and every CAS number is checked before requests begin. Each returned structure is validated before its definition is saved.

Text files contain one CAS number per line and allow comments starting with #: 

# Substances to import
50-78-2
71-43-2
64-17-5

A JSON file contains an array of strings:

["50-78-2", "71-43-2", "64-17-5"]

In Minecraft:

/avogadro cas import-list chemicals.txt
/avogadro cas import-list chemicals.json
/avogadro cas import-list ["50-78-2","71-43-2","64-17-5"]

In the console, quote the array to keep it together:

import-list '["50-78-2","71-43-2","64-17-5"]'

Find saved files

By default, definitions are saved using the selected substance name:

config/avogadro/server/data/imported/molecules/<name>.json

Original CAS detail responses are kept separately, with provenance metadata:

data/avogadro/cas/<CAS RN>.json

cache open prints the cache directory. cache clear --yes removes cached responses and their metadata while keeping imported molecule definitions. After importing, reload the server's molecule resources to make the definitions available.

Check or cancel an operation

In Minecraft and the interactive console, status shows whether an operation is running, and cancel requests cancellation. Closing the console cancels its current operation. Completed definition files are kept. When passing a command directly to the launcher instead of opening its console, it runs in the foreground; use Ctrl+C to stop the process.

CAS data and access

Check the applicable CAS terms before redistributing imported data. Preserve its attribution and license information. See CAS Common Chemistry, CC BY-NC 4.0, and the API access and renewal form.
